Specifically, the market's implied probability of an October hike is now under 20%; that of a 25 bps December hike is near 90%, and 2.5 hikes are priced in by mid-2027.
#economy #markets #federalreserve

tweets.text:
One of the misconceptions that is parroted on CT is that "trading" memecoins is trading. 

It isn't. 

Nowadays, unlike the past, the very successful people doing this are either social engineers (monetizing their social audience via callouts, selling into tweets, insider knowledge, selling with side wallets, creating coins to dump and pretending it isn't them etc.), or sophisticated devs who are able to build tools to systematically extract from gamblers via bots (this is edge).

There are some moments where trading comes into it, when something becomes liquid or distributed enough, but doing very well in the trenches isn't the same skillset as actual trading, and I think calling it trading is personally misleading and unhelpful. 

If you can't trade large real liquid assets then you should not drop out to do this, as your luck will eventually run out, or you will end up turning to onchain crime, which is bad for your soul and no way to live. 

I also think the people that are able to run it up big in memecoins are unable to keep that money, because those two things are at odds with each other. The person that can run it up and not TP due to delusional optimism, is unable to sell usually. There are probably only one or two people I knew that made it big with memes that were able to step away and keep that money (@blockgraze is one). Everyone else thought they could repeat the process and ruined themselves eventually. 

I think it is fine to bet on yourself and take some big swings in life, but this isn't the right path. I'm not trying to shit on anyone's dreams, but full time gambling isn't the one.

One of the misconceptions that is parroted on CT is that "trading" memecoins is trading. 

It isn't. 

Nowadays, unlike the past, the very successful people doing this are either social engineers (monetizing their social audience via callouts, selling into tweets, insider knowledge, selling with side wallets, creating coins to dump and pretending it isn't them etc.), or sophisticated devs who are able to build tools to systematically extract from gamblers via bots (this is edge).

There are some moments where trading comes into it, when something becomes liquid or distributed enough, but doing very well in the trenches isn't the same skillset as actual trading, and I think calling it trading is personally misleading and unhelpful. 

If you can't trade large real liquid assets then you should not drop out to do this, as your luck will eventually run out, or you will end up turning to onchain crime, which is bad for your soul and no way to live. 

I also think the people that are able to run it up big in memecoins are unable to keep that money, because those two things are at odds with each other. The person that can run it up and not TP due to delusional optimism, is unable to sell usually. There are probably only one or two people I knew that made it big with memes that were able to step away and keep that money (@blockgraze is one). Everyone else thought they could repeat the process and ruined themselves eventually. 

I think it is fine to bet on yourself and take some big swings in life, but this isn't the right path. I'm not trying to shit on anyone's dreams, but full time gambling isn't the one.
